results.reason: Identifies Sched. §1.1 (ship date from Supplier's plant) vs. MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester). Explains that a shipment sent on time but arriving late counts as on time, undercutting §5.2 remedies. Also covers risk passing at shipment and the invoice/payment clock starting at shipment.
Recommends conforming the Schedule's Delivery Date definition to MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester) and adding an order-of-precedence clause.

Identifies MSA §4.3 as covering all housings and similar components worldwide, versus Term Sheet Series 7 / US only. Explains the lock-in and the bar on cover purchases elsewhere. Recommends narrowing to Series 7 Housings in the US.

Identifies §15.2 free assignment by Supplier while Customer needs consent. Explains the risk of a competing or unknown assignee holding exclusivity and the Specifications. Recommends consent, a no-competitor bar and a change-of-control termination right.

Identifies that Amendment §2.1 restates §11.2 to exclude only willful misconduct, which brings gross negligence and the IP indemnity under the 12-month-fees cap. Recommends restoring the original §11.2(a)–(c).
States the cap as fees paid in the prior 12 months (§11.1) and lists the original exclusions as gross negligence, willful misconduct and the IP indemnity.
States that Term Sheet §§3.1–3.3 limit exclusivity to Series 7 Housings in the US and uses this as the baseline against MSA §4.3.

Header cites New York law (MSA §16.1). The memo frames the NY public-policy point as unverified and has an assumptions section. Its UCC references are real provisions, not invented ones, and are expressly flagged 'to be confirmed'. No cases are cited.
The memo is addressed to the partner and goes issue by issue with Where, Why it matters and Fix for each. Issues are in priority order, and there is a dedicated assumptions and facts-needed section.

The Term Sheet is used only as evidence of the agreed deal and as negotiating leverage. The memo does not flag the 3-year term or the 45-day payment terms as defects; it expressly calls the 45-day dispute window 'not a departure'.

Section citations for exclusivity (§4.3), assignment (§15.2) and the cap (§11) are accurate, and the beneficiary analysis is correct. External authority is limited to UCC references, which are flagged for verification.
